w-jp-014.title: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup

w-jp-014-i1.name: Eggs
w-jp-014-i1.standardAmount: 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

w-jp-014-i8.name: Soy Sauce
w-jp-014-i8.standardAmount: 1½ Tbsp (use gluten-free soy sauce for GF)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Beat 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell) in a measuring cup or in a bowl with a spout.
instructions.3: Cut the white part of 2 green onions/scallions into thin round pieces. Then, thinly slice the green part diagonally. Set them aside separately.
instructions.4: Cut 3.5 oz medium-firm tofu (momen dofu) into ½-inch (1.3 cm) cubes.
instructions.5: Add 2 Tbsp dried wakame seaweed to a small bowl of water and rehydrate for 5 minutes. Then, drain and squeeze the water out. Set aside.
instructions.6: Preheat a medium pot over medium heat. When the pot is hot, add 2 tsp roasted sesame oil, then the white part of the green onions.
instructions.7: Stir-fry for 30 seconds until the green onions are well coated with the oil. Then, add 2 cups chicken stock/broth and 2 cups water.
instructions.8: Add 1½ Tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, and ¼ tsp white pepper powder.
instructions.9: After mixing the soup well, cover the pot with a lid and bring it to a boil.
instructions.10: Once boiling, add the tofu and 1 oz dried glass/cellophane noodles (harusame).
instructions.11: Cook the glass noodles according to the package instructions. Stir the noodles in the beginning so they don’t stick to each other or the bottom of the pot.
instructions.12: After the noodles are cooked, adjust the heat so the soup is simmering (a very gentle boil). Slowly pour a steady trickle of the beaten eggs into the soup in a circular motion, starting from the center and spiraling outward. (Don’t pour on top of any egg that you’ve already added to the soup.) Place cooking chopsticks at the edge of the bowl/measuring cup while pouring so the egg will drizzle down the chopsticks in a thin stream. Let the eggs sit without stirring for 20–25 seconds until they’re fluffy and just cooked.
instructions.13: Add the rehydrated wakame seaweed, green parts of the green onions, and 2 tsp toasted white sesame seeds. Remove the saucepan from the heat to prevent overcooking.
instructions.14: Transfer the glass noodles to individual bowls with a pair of tongs. Then pour the soup and other ingredients over the noodles. Serve hot.

w-jp-014.culturalNotes: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup is a popular dish in Japan, often served as a light meal or part of a lunch.

w-jp-015.title: Kamaboko with Salmon Roe

instructions.1: Remove the kamaboko from the refrigerator and let it thaw if frozen.
instructions.2: Wash the shiso leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.3: Place the kamaboko on a serving plate.
instructions.4: Sprinkle the chopped shiso leaves over the surface of the kamaboko.
instructions.5: Add the salmon roe on top of the shiso leaves.

w-jp-015.culturalNotes: Kamaboko is a traditional Japanese fish cake, often served as an appetizer on special occasions.

w-jp-016.title: Karaage Chicken Salad

instructions.1: In a small bowl, mix together all the chilli dressing ingredients then set aside.
instructions.2: Wash the green salad leaves and spin to remove the excess water.
instructions.3: Cut the tomatoes into quarters and set aside.
instructions.4: Slice the red onion thinly and soak in water for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Drain the water and spin the sliced onion to remove excess water completely.
instructions.6: In a large bowl, place the salad leaves, cherry tomatoes, sliced red onion, and karaage chicken.
instructions.7: Pour the chilli dressing over the salad.
instructions.8: Garnish the salad with crushed peanuts and chopped coriander as desired.

w-jp-016.culturalNotes: Karaage is a popular Japanese fried chicken dish, often used in salads and as a snack.

w-jp-017.title: Japanese Korokke

instructions.1: Peel and dice the potatoes.
instructions.2: Cook the potatoes in boiling water for about 10 minutes.
instructions.3: While the potatoes are cooking, finely chop the onion and carrot and set aside.
instructions.4: Heat olive oil in a frying pan over high heat and add the ground beef to cook.
instructions.5: When the color of most of the ground beef changes, add the onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.6: Check if the potatoes are cooked by inserting a skewer. If it goes through, the potatoes are cooked.
instructions.7: Strain the water from the potatoes, put them back in the pot, and shake them around to rough up the outsides a little.
instructions.8: Mash the potatoes with a potato masher while they are warm.
instructions.9: Add the cooked ground beef, onion, and carrot to the mashed potatoes and combine them well.
instructions.10: Divide the mixture into 8 equal-sized flat ovals.
instructions.11: Combine the egg, water, mayonnaise, and flour in a small bowl to make a batter.
instructions.12: Coat each oval with the batter, then place the potato oval into the panko crumbs.
instructions.13: Coat all potato ovals with the panko crumbs.
instructions.14: Heat deep frying oil in a deep pan until it reaches around 180°C (350°F).
instructions.15: Fry each potato oval until crispy and golden brown.
instructions.16: Serve the korokke with salad leaves or any side dish of your choice.

w-jp-017.culturalNotes: Korokke is a popular dish in Japan, consisting of fried croquettes made from mashed potatoes and ground beef.

w-jp-018.title: Kuromitsu (Black Sugar Syrup)

instructions.1: In a small saucepan, mix 3.5 oz of black sugar, ½ cup of granulated sugar (to taste), and ½ cup of water.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat. Tip: This kuromitsu is quite rich, so feel free to reduce the amount of granulated sugar or omit it entirely, to your preference.
instructions.3: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring gently until the sugar dissolves completely and the mixture thickens slightly.
instructions.4: Allow it to cool and transfer to an airtight jar. Keep in the refrigerator for up to a week.

w-jp-018.culturalNotes: Kuromitsu (black sugar syrup) is a rich, sweet liquid used in many traditional Japanese desserts.

w-jp-019.title: Manjū

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. Cut a sheet of parchment paper into 12 pieces, each 2.5 × 2.5 inches (6 × 6 cm).
instructions.2: In a small saucepan, add 3 Tbsp of water and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. Whisk to dissolve the sugar over medium-low heat.
instructions.3: Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and set aside to cool.
instructions.4: While the mixture is cooling, wet your hands with a little bit of water and make 12 balls of sweet red bean paste. Each ball should be about 20 grams.
instructions.5: Combine 1/2 tsp of baking powder with 1/2 tsp of water.
instructions.6: Add the baking powder mixture to the cooled brown sugar mixture and mix well.
instructions.7: Sift 1 cup of cake flour and add it to the brown sugar mixture. Combine the ingredients using a silicone spatula, chopsticks, or your fingers. Form the dough into a ball. Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.8: Transfer the dough to a floured work surface and knead for 1-2 minutes, adding flour as needed to prevent sticking. The dough should be smooth and pliable.
instructions.9: Shape the dough into a stick and cut it into 12 pieces.
instructions.10: Cover the pieces with a damp towel to prevent them from drying out.
instructions.11: Shape one piece of dough into a ball and flatten it to a diameter of 2 inches (5 cm). Flatten the piece with your fingers and roll it out to form a circle about 2.5 to 3 inches (6-7 cm) in diameter. Only stretch the outer edges of the dough and keep the center thick.
instructions.12: Place a ball of sweet red bean paste in the center and pull the edges to the center, pinching to seal the dough.
instructions.13: Place the manju on the work surface, seam side down. Rotate the dough a few times to shape it nicely. Place it on the parchment paper.
instructions.15: Set up a steamer. Fill the wok (or pot) with 2 inches of water and bring it to a boil. Steam the manju for 10-12 minutes on high heat.

w-jp-019.culturalNotes: Manjū is a traditional Japanese sweet made from a brown sugar dough and a sweet red bean paste filling.

w-jp-020.title: Egg and Spinach Miso Soup

instructions.1: Boil the water in a saucepan and add the dashi powder (or boil homemade dashi).
instructions.2: Add the miso paste and dissolve it into the dashi.
instructions.3: Lower the heat and add the eggs and spinach.
instructions.4: Simmer for a few minutes until the eggs and spinach are just cooked (try not to overcook).
instructions.5: Serve in small bowls and garnish with shallots if desired (optional).

w-jp-020.culturalNotes: Miso soup is a staple of the traditional Japanese breakfast, typically served with rice and fish.

w-jp-021.title: Monjayaki

w-jp-021-i3.name: Bull Dog Vegetable & Fruit Tonkatsu Sauce

w-jp-021-i18.name: Vegetable baby star ramen or any ramen snack

instructions.1: In a medium-sized bowl, dissolve the kombu dashi granules in the water. Add the tonkatsu sauce, flour, salt, and pepper and stir well.
instructions.2: Add the cabbage, agedama, and add-ins from section A. Mix it together.
instructions.3: Scoop out the cabbage and add-ins and cook on the griddle until the cabbage is softened. Make a donut shape and then slowly pour in the remaining batter along with any add-ins from 'B'.
instructions.4: When it starts to cook, mix it all together. When the color changes and it is 80% done, spread it flat.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with toppings of choice. Let it thicken to your liking, then use a scraper (or spoon) to serve. Press the scraper down to achieve a crispy bottom.

w-jp-021.culturalNotes: Monjayaki is a popular dish in Japan, especially in Tokyo. It is typically served on a special griddle and eaten directly from the griddle using a wooden spatula.

w-jp-022.title: Pickled Daikon and Carrot (Kōhaku Namasu)

instructions.1: Wash the daikon and carrot.
instructions.2: Peel the daikon and carrot. Cut them into thin julienne strips about 2-3 inches long using a sharp knife or a mandoline slicer.
instructions.3: Place the julienned daikon and carrot in a bowl. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of salt and gently mix. Let it sit for about 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Squeeze the excess water out of the daikon and carrot with your hands, then discard the water and return the daikon and carrot to the bowl.
instructions.5: In a small mixing bowl, combine the vinegar and sugar until the sugar dissolves completely.
instructions.6: Pour the vinaigrette over the daikon and carrot. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to an hour.
instructions.7: Before serving, give the namasu a gentle stir. You can garnish it with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds if desired.
instructions.8: Serve as a side along with other dishes.

w-jp-022.culturalNotes: Namasu is a traditional Japanese side dish served on special occasions and during Christmas.

w-jp-023.title: Hiroshima Okonomiyaki

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix water, plain flour, and dashi powder until the batter is smooth.
instructions.2: Add a drop of vegetable oil and bonito flakes, and mix well.
instructions.3: Add shredded cabbage, chopped scallions, bean sprouts, tempura crisps, and seaweed flakes, and mix well.
instructions.4: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add olive oil.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the skillet and cook until golden brown on the bottom.
instructions.6: Add the yakisoba noodles and gently mix.
instructions.7: Crack the eggs over the batter and cover the skillet for 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked.
instructions.8: Gently flip the batter and cook the other side until done.

w-jp-023.culturalNotes: Hiroshima Okonomiyaki is a popular dish in Japan, especially in Hiroshima. It is known for its thick, rich layers.

w-jp-024.title: Omurice

instructions.1: Cut the chicken, onion, and carrot into small cubes.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
instructions.3: Add the chicken to the pan and cook until the meat has all turned white.
instructions.4: Add the vegetables and cook until the onion becomes translucent.
instructions.5: Add the ketchup and mix it all together.
instructions.6: Add the rice and mix until the rice is all coated with the ketchup.
instructions.7: Add the thawed frozen peas and mix them with the rice and ketchup.
instructions.8: Flavor with salt and pepper to taste.
instructions.9: Remove from heat and set aside in a large bowl.
instructions.10: In a small bowl, crack and beat 2 eggs.
instructions.11: Heat the large frying pan over medium heat and add 1/2 tbsp of olive oil, then pour in the eggs, allowing them to spread all over the bottom of the pan and slightly scramble the middle without breaking the omelette.
instructions.12: Turn off the heat, and pour half the ketchup rice into the center of the omelette.
instructions.13: Push the omelette and rice to one side of the pan and fold in the sides of the omelette to wrap the rice.
instructions.14: Hold a plate beside the omelette and tip the pan a bit to slide the omelette onto the plate so that it flips onto the plate with the egg on top covering the rice.
instructions.15: Repeat these steps again for the next 2 eggs and remaining chicken rice, then serve!

w-jp-024.culturalNotes: Omurice is a popular Japanese dish that combines rice, chicken, and eggs, often served on family occasions.

w-jp-025.title: Onigiri

instructions.1: Wash the rice and cook it according to the package or rice cooker instructions. Let it cool until it can be handled with your hands.
instructions.2: While the rice is cooking, prepare your fillings.
instructions.3: Fill a bowl with salt water to rinse your fingers and season the onigiri.
instructions.4: Use one of the two methods to shape the onigiri:
instructions.5: Method 1: Wet your hands in the salt water. Take two large spoonfuls of rice into one hand (carefully; the rice is hot), and gently squeeze and flatten it with the other. Make an indentation in the middle, and put some of the filling into the center. Be a little careful to get the filling only in the center and not all over the ball; that can make the rice less sticky, and stickiness is good. 'Fold' the rice over the filling so it becomes covered. Squeeze gently, and mold it into a triangular shape by folding both your hands along the palms while keeping the fingers straight. Squeeze like that, rotating the ball a few times, and you will soon have a very neat triangle—this really is much harder to explain than to do. Once the ball is done, put it down on a clean surface to cool down. Rinse your hands in the salt water and repeat.
instructions.6: Method 2: Use a bowl and some plastic film. Place about ⅔ of the mixture into the center of the cling wrap that has been draped into the bowl loosely. Then, add approximately 2 teaspoons of filling (this is working off of about 3–4 portions per cup of rice). Then, place the last ⅓ of the rice to the top. Then, mold the onigiri within the cling wrap. This drastically reduces mess and also is slightly more 'kid friendly'.
instructions.7: Once the balls are reasonably cool, you need to protect them from drying out. The easiest way is to wrap them in cling wrap, or put them into an airtight plastic food container. When it is time to eat, take one rice ball, wrap it in a piece of nori, and eat away. If you don't mind soggy nori, you can wrap the balls in nori beforehand.

w-jp-025.culturalNotes: Onigiri is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish, often served with various fillings and wrapped in nori sheets.

w-jp-026.title: Cabbage and Onsen Tamago Miso Soup

w-jp-026-i6.name: large eggs
w-jp-026-i6.standardAmount: 3 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. I made 2 onsen tamago (silky poached eggs) today.
instructions.2: Remove the core of ¼ onion and cut into thin slices.
instructions.3: To a medium saucepan, add 3 cups water, the sliced onion, and 2 dashi packets. Cover the saucepan with a lid and bring it to a boil on medium heat.
instructions.4: Remove the core of ⅛ head green cabbage and cut into small, ¾-inch (2-cm) squares. Discard any tough, dense pieces or reserve them for other recipes. Alternatively, you can add them to the saucepan earlier than the leafy parts to give them extra time to cook and soften.
instructions.5: Cut 1 green onion/scallion in half widthwise and diagonally cut into thin slices.
instructions.6: Once the water is boiling, shake the dashi packets with cooking chopsticks to release more flavor. Reduce the heat to medium low and cook, covered, for 4-5 minutes. Then, discard the dashi packets.
instructions.7: Add the cabbage and cook, covered, until both the onion and cabbage are tender, about 4-5 minutes.
instructions.8: To make the onsen tamago: Place the eggs in a bowl of hot water (about 65-70°C) for 12-15 minutes.
instructions.9: Add the miso to the soup and stir well.
instructions.10: Serve the soup hot with the onsen tamago and sliced green onion. You can add shichimi togarashi and Japanese sansho pepper to taste.

w-jp-026.culturalNotes: Onsen tamago is a traditional Japanese dish served in Japanese hot springs. It is slowly cooked in warm water to give it a silky texture.

w-jp-027.title: Cold Somen Noodles with Sudachi Lime

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. If using homemade shiro dashi instead of store-bought, you will need to prepare ice cubes instead of the iced water shown in the image. In addition, you can prepare several more ice cubes to add to the serving bowls if you prefer your noodles extra chilled (optional).
instructions.2: Thinly slice all but 1 of the 5 sudachi (or 2-3 limes) and set aside for garnish. Cut the 1 remaining sudachi in half widthwise and reserve for juicing.
instructions.3: Prepare the Ice-Cold Soup Broth: Mix shiro dashi with iced water to make 1⅔ cups of the cold broth.
instructions.4: Cook the Somen Noodles: Place the somen in boiling water for 5 minutes until cooked. Drain the noodles and rinse them with cold water.
instructions.5: Assemble and Serve: Place the noodles in serving bowls and add the cold broth. Garnish with sliced sudachi and serve cold.

w-jp-027.culturalNotes: Somen is a type of thin Japanese noodle that is typically served cold in the summer.

w-jp-028.title: Chocolate Salt Bread

w-jp-028-i12.name: rock salt, pearl salt, or flaky salt

instructions.1: Mix the bread flour, cake flour, cocoa powder, skim milk powder, sugar, instant dry yeast, and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the water and mix the ingredients well.
instructions.3: Add the unsalted butter and mix until the dough becomes cohesive.
instructions.4: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Divide the dough into 6 equal parts and shape each part into a ball.
instructions.6: Place a piece of salted butter and chocolate in the center of each ball and seal it.
instructions.7: Place the balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and let them rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.8: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius.
instructions.9: Bake the bread for 20 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.10: Remove the bread from the oven and sprinkle with rock salt, pearl salt, or flaky salt.
instructions.11: Let the bread cool before serving.

w-jp-028.culturalNotes: Chocolate salt bread is a popular Japanese bread, known for its rich, sweet, and salty flavor.

w-jp-029.title: Japanese Sashimi

instructions.1: Using a very sharp knife, cut the pieces of fish against the grain to about 1/4 inch slices or less.
instructions.2: Arrange the fish on a Japanese tray along with a bunch of shredded daikon radish, some wasabi, and ginger slices.
instructions.3: It is customary to serve with a small dish for the soy sauce, and guests will mix the wasabi with the soy sauce to the desired amount of heat.
instructions.4: The ginger is used to cleanse the palate between different bites.

w-jp-029.culturalNotes: Sashimi is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of carefully sliced raw fish served with complementary ingredients such as wasabi and pickled ginger.

w-jp-030.title: Shiruko (Sweet Red Bean Soup)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. Make the Shiratama Dango ahead (15 minutes) or toast kirimochi instead.
instructions.2: Add 7 oz of sweet red bean paste (anko) to a saucepan. Pour in half of the water.
instructions.3: Mash the anko with a spatula until no lumps remain.
instructions.4: Pour in the rest of the water and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Once simmering, cook for 1-2 minutes. Add a pinch of salt (optional).
instructions.5: Serve the sweet red bean soup with the Shiratama Dango.

w-jp-030.culturalNotes: Shiruko is a traditional Japanese dessert usually served in winter. It is known for its sweet taste and creamy texture.

w-jp-031.title: Green Shiso Juice

instructions.1: Wash the shiso leaves thoroughly and chop them into small pieces.
instructions.2: Add the chopped shiso leaves to a blender with water, sugar, and apple cider vinegar.
instructions.3: Blend the ingredients until smooth and liquid.
instructions.4: Strain the juice using a fine mesh sieve to remove the leaves and any debris.
instructions.5: Serve the juice chilled, with ice cubes if desired.

w-jp-031.culturalNotes: Shiso is a herb commonly used in Japanese cuisine to add a unique and refreshing flavor.

w-jp-032.title: Soba

instructions.1: Place the dried soba noodles in a shallow container and add enough water to cover the noodles for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: While the noodles are soaking, start to boil 12 cups of water in a large pot over high heat.
instructions.3: Add the vegetable oil to the pot.
instructions.4: Remove the noodles from the soaking water and put them into the boiling water.
instructions.5: Cook the noodles for 3 minutes.
instructions.6: Turn the heat off and drain the cooking water.
instructions.7: Wash the cooked noodles under running water.
instructions.8: Your noodles are ready to make a salad or serve cold or warm.

w-jp-032.culturalNotes: Soba is a type of Japanese noodle made from buckwheat flour, typically served cold in the summer or warm in the winter.

w-jp-033.title: Taiyaki

instructions.1: Divide the sweet red bean paste into 6 equal parts (40 g each) and shape them into 10 cm long cylinders using plastic wrap. Set aside.
instructions.2: Sift the flour and baking powder into a large bowl and make a well in the center.
instructions.3: In another bowl, beat the egg lightly before adding milk and water. Mix everything thoroughly until smooth.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into the well of flour. Combine them but try not to overmix.
instructions.5: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 30 minutes to rest the batter.
instructions.6: Heat the taiyaki pan over low-medium heat and pour about 2 tablespoons of batter into the bottom side of the pan. Pour the batter from the top edge so that it dribbles down to the bottom of the pan.
instructions.7: Place a roll of sweet red bean paste in the center and pour more batter (about 2 tablespoons) over the paste.
instructions.8: Press the pan and cook each side for 3-5 minutes over low heat.
instructions.9: When both sides are cooked, remove the taiyaki carefully.
instructions.10: Repeat the process with the remaining batter and Anko.

w-jp-033.culturalNotes: Taiyaki is a traditional Japanese sweet made in a special fish-shaped pan. It is usually eaten hot and often found in public places and markets.

w-jp-034.title: Takoyaki

instructions.1: Mix water, egg, and dashi stock in a bowl and whisk well until frothy.
instructions.2: Sift the flour into a large bowl and add the liquid mixture over the flour.
instructions.3: Whisk them together well until all the dry flour is completely mixed in.
instructions.4: Heat the takoyaki pan and oil the holes with the oil brush.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the holes so they are approximately 80% full, then add the octopus, green onion, tempura crisps, and pickled ginger. Add more of the batter until it's just overflowing.
instructions.6: Cook for approximately 1.5 minutes, then trim off the excess batter and flip them over by inserting the takoyaki pick from the 4 o'clock direction, turn your wrist 90°.
instructions.7: Keep flipping them around until the takoyaki are a golden-brown color.
instructions.8: When all balls are crispy golden brown, turn the heat off.
instructions.9: Serve them on a plate and coat with the takoyaki sauce and Japanese mayonnaise, then sprinkle with aonori and bonito flakes.

w-jp-034.culturalNotes: Takoyaki is a popular dish in Japan, served as an appetizer in restaurants and markets.

w-jp-035.title: Tamago Kake Gohan

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. For the steamed rice, ¾ cup (150 g) of uncooked Japanese short-grain rice yields 2¼ US cups (330 g) of cooked white rice.
instructions.2: Add 1 serving of cooked Japanese short-grain rice to a rice bowl. The rice should be steaming hot.
instructions.3: Make a well in the middle of the rice. Crack 1 large egg (50 g without shell) into the well.
instructions.4: Drizzle a small amount of soy sauce onto the egg.
instructions.5: Add toppings of your choice. I like to sprinkle katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes) around the egg in the rice.
instructions.6: Drizzle a bit more soy sauce on the toppings if you wish.
instructions.7: Stir the ingredients with a pair of chopsticks until the egg is fully incorporated into the rice and turns a pale yellow color.
instructions.8: Enjoy!

w-jp-035.culturalNotes: Tamago Kake Gohan is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish often served in the morning. It is known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-jp-036.title: Tamagoyaki

instructions.1: Crack the eggs into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Add the seasonings (shirodashi and water for dashimaki or sugar, salt, and water for atsumaki) and mix them together gently to avoid too much bubble formation.
instructions.3: Strain the egg mixture through a sieve a few times.
instructions.4: Pour about 2 tbsp of oil into a small bowl and soak kitchen paper and set aside.
instructions.5: Heat 2 tsp of olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat until you can feel the heat when you hover your hand over the pan.
instructions.6: Pour 1/3 of the egg mixture into the pan (you should hear a sizzling sound).
instructions.7: Break any bubbles that have formed with the edge of the chopsticks and scramble gently.
instructions.8: When the surface is solidified a little, fold and push the egg to one end of the pan with chopsticks.
instructions.9: Wipe the empty side of the pan with oil-soaked kitchen paper and pour another 1/3 of the egg mixture into the empty space of the pan.
instructions.10: Lift the folded egg up to let the egg mixture run under it.
instructions.11: Fold and roll the egg from one side of the pan and wipe the empty space of the pan with the oil-soaked kitchen paper.
instructions.12: Pour the last 1/3 of the egg mixture and repeat fold and roll.
instructions.13: Turn the heat off and wrap the rolled egg with a thin kitchen towel.
instructions.14: Roll the wrapped egg roll with a sushi mat to shape and rest to cool down.
instructions.15: Once it is cooled down, slice it 2 cm (0.79 inch) thick and serve.

w-jp-036.culturalNotes: Tamagoyaki is a type of Japanese rolled omelette often served in daily meals.

w-jp-037.title: Tuna Tataki

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Grate the ginger and collect 1 tsp ginger (grated, with juice). Slice 1 green onion/scallion thinly and set aside.
instructions.3: Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl: the green onions, the grated ginger, 3 Tbsp ponzu, 2 tsp roasted sesame oil, 1 tsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp toasted white sesame seeds. Set aside.
instructions.4: Heat a nonstick frying pan. When the pan is hot, add 2 Tbsp neutral oil. When the oil is hot, add 225 g sashimi-grade yellowfin/ahi tuna and sear it 30 seconds on each side.
instructions.5: When all sides are seared, remove from the heat and let it cool. Slice the tuna into ¼-inch (6-mm) pieces. Pour the sauce on the Tuna Tataki and serve with ½ lemon and Korean chili thread.

w-jp-037.culturalNotes: Tuna Tataki is a traditional Japanese dish often served as a starter or light main course. It is known for its strong and delicious flavor.

w-jp-038.title: Japanese Kakiage Tempura

instructions.1: Cut the onion, carrot, and sweet potato into small pieces.
instructions.2: Wash the shiso leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.3: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the water gradually and mix until you get a thick batter.
instructions.5: Add the vegetables and shiso leaves to the batter and mix well.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 170 degrees Celsius.
instructions.7: Add a tablespoon of the batter mixture to the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
instructions.8: Remove the kakiage from the oil and place it on a paper towel to drain excess oil.
instructions.9: Repeat the process until all the mixture is used up.

w-jp-038.culturalNotes: Kakiage is a type of Japanese tempura, consisting of small vegetable pieces fried in a batter.

w-jp-039.title: Buri Teriyaki

instructions.1: Prepare the yellowtail fish fillet. Sprinkle salt and leave it for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: After 15 minutes, wipe the excess liquid off the fish with paper towels.
instructions.3: Heat the butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
instructions.4: Fry the fish on both sides until brown.
instructions.5: Turn up the heat and pour the teriyaki sauce over the fish.
instructions.6: Cook until the sauce has reduced and become thick and shiny.
instructions.7: Turn off the heat and serve the fish with a shiso leaf and radish.

w-jp-039.culturalNotes: Teriyaki is a traditional Japanese dish characterized by its sweet and salty teriyaki sauce.

w-jp-040.title: Katsu Sauce

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Combine 4½ Tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 2 Tbsp sugar in a jar or small bowl and whisk until the sugar dissolves.
instructions.3: Add 5 Tbsp ketchup and 2 Tbsp oyster sauce and whisk until incorporated.
instructions.4: Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed. The sauce is now ready to use.
instructions.5: For a thicker sauce, refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

w-jp-040.culturalNotes: A sweet-savoury sauce served with katsu, breaded fried cutlets of chicken or beef, a popular dish in Japan.

w-jp-042.title: Tsukemono-Nukazuke (Rice Bran Pickle)

instructions.1: Boil the water to remove chlorine and set aside to cool down.
instructions.2: Place the roasted rice bran into the container used for pickling.
instructions.3: Add salt to the roasted rice bran and mix them well.
instructions.4: Pour the cooled down water into the container and mix them well with hands.
instructions.5: Press the kelp and chili into the rice bran bed and bury them completely.
instructions.6: Make the top surface flat with your hands, wipe the container to clean (avoiding other bacteria growth) and place a lid on.
instructions.7: Refrigerate to rest overnight.
instructions.8: Next morning, take the container out of the fridge and press the cabbage leaves into the rice bran pickling bed (nukadoko) and bury them completely with rice bran.
instructions.9: Wipe the inside of the container with wet cloths to clean.
instructions.10: Place the lid and leave it overnight at room temperature.
instructions.11: Next day, remove the cabbage leaves out of the rice bran bed, and stir the rice bran bed well.
instructions.12: Add another cabbage leaf, cover with the rice bran, flatten the top surface and wipe off to clean the container with wet cloths.
instructions.13: Repeat the above process 3-4 times in order to mature the rice bran pickling bed.
instructions.14: After you repeat the above process 3-4 times, the rice bran bed is ready to pickle.
instructions.15: Wash the vegetables that you want to pickle and prep the vegetables.

w-jp-042.culturalNotes: Tsukemono-Nukazuke is a traditional Japanese pickle that uses roasted rice bran as the base for pickling.

w-jp-043.title: Curry Udon

instructions.1: Slice the beef very thinly and chop the onion.
instructions.2: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in an oven-proof frying pan over medium heat.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion and cook for a few minutes.
instructions.4: Add the beef and cook until the color changes.
instructions.5: Add 2 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Remove the scum as necessary.
instructions.6: Open and empty the Udon soup packet into the frying pan.
instructions.7: Add 2 pieces of curry roux.
instructions.8: When the curry roux has dissolved and the soup has thickened, turn off the heat.
instructions.9: In a separate pot, bring 2 liters of water to a boil and add the udon noodles and cook for one minute.
instructions.10: Turn off the heat and drain the cooking water.
instructions.11: Serve half of the udon noodles in a bowl and pour half of the curry soup.

w-jp-043.culturalNotes: Curry Udon is a popular dish in Japan, served as a warm and comforting meal on cold days.

w-jp-044.title: Umeboshi Onigiri (Pickled Plum Rice Balls)

instructions.1: Rinse the rice and cook it according to your usual method.
instructions.2: Once cooked, gently fluff the rice and let it cool just enough to handle safely. Keep it warm because warm rice is easier to shape.
instructions.3: Remove the stones from the umeboshi and roughly mash the umeboshi flesh.
instructions.4: Weigh the cooked rice and divide it into 2 portions of approximately 120 g (4 oz) each.
instructions.5: Wet both hands lightly with water to prevent the rice from sticking.
instructions.6: Place a pinch of salt in one palm, then rub your hands together to spread it evenly.
instructions.7: Place half of the onigiri portion (60 g / 2 oz) in your palm and gently flatten it.
instructions.8: Make a small indentation in the center and add the umeboshi filling.
instructions.9: Cover it with the remaining rice, making sure the filling stays enclosed in the center.
instructions.10: Cup the rice gently between your hands and shape it into a triangle.
instructions.11: Use just enough pressure for the grains to hold together, rather than squeezing or packing the rice tightly.
instructions.12: Wrap a strip or sheet of nori around the finished umeboshi onigiri.

w-jp-044.culturalNotes: Umeboshi onigiri is a traditional Japanese dish often served as a snack or part of a breakfast meal.

w-mx-001.title: Mexican Adobo

instructions.1: Toast the guajillo chiles in a dry medium hot pan for about 30 seconds per side until they are fragrant and pliable.
instructions.2: When the chiles are cool to the touch, remove the seeds and stems and discard.
instructions.3: Place the toasted chiles in a pan and just barely cover with water. Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and let the chiles soak for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Roughly chop the tomatoes and onion.
instructions.5: In a preheated skillet with 3 tbsp of cooking oil, blacken the tomato, onion, and garlic.
instructions.6: Add the reconstituted chiles, tomato, onion, garlic, and 1/4 cup of the soaking liquid to a blender. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
instructions.7: Preheat a skillet with 4 tbsp of cooking oil, then pour the blended mixture into the skillet. Add the vinegar and sugar. Stir to incorporate.
instructions.8: Cook until most of the liquid has evaporated from the adobo and it forms peaks when you pass a spoon through it.
instructions.9: Allow it to rest for 2 hours while the chicken is marinating.

w-mx-001.culturalNotes: Mexican adobo is a spicy and aromatic sauce used in many traditional Mexican dishes.

w-mx-002.title: Aguachile Rojo

instructions.1: Combine the shrimp, lime juice, salt, and black pepper in a large shallow bowl or baking dish. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, stirring halfway through to ensure the shrimp is evenly coated.
instructions.2: In a large cast-iron skillet or comal over medium heat, add the guajillo, árbol, and pequín chiles and toast for 1-2 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the chiles are puffed and fragrant. They will darken in color, but make sure not to burn them completely.
instructions.3: Transfer the chiles to a small saucepan. Add enough water to cover them completely and bring to a boil over high heat. Remove the pan from the heat, cover, and let them soak for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Transfer the softened chiles to a small blender using a slotted spoon. Add the garlic, Jugo Maggi, Worcestershire sauce, and fresh water. Blend until completely smooth.
instructions.5: Pour the chile sauce into the dish with the shrimp and stir until well combined. Cover and refrigerate for an additional 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Stir in the cucumber, mango, red onion, and cilantro until combined. Taste and season with more salt as needed. Serve immediately with tostadas, chips, or saltine crackers.

w-mx-002.culturalNotes: Aguachile is a popular dish in Mexico, especially in the state of Sinaloa, where it is served as a fresh and flavorful appetizer.

w-mx-003.title: Alfajor (Hispanoamérica)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cornstarch, and orange zest.
instructions.3: In another bowl, beat egg yolks until pale yellow.
instructions.4: Add dry ingredients to egg yolks in three parts, mixing the orange juice in between. If the dough seems sticky, add extra cornstarch one tablespoon at a time, until the dough comes together and is no longer sticky.
instructions.5: Roll the dough out thinly (about 3 mm). Only roll one side of the dough or else it won’t curl when baked.
instructions.6: Cut out the shapes and prick with a fork so they won't puff up.
instructions.7: Bake for 4-7 minutes. Do not let them brown. They should remain soft and tender. Let cool.
instructions.8: Spread with dulce de leche. Put two halves together and enjoy. Dust with powdered sugar if desired.

w-mx-003.culturalNotes: Alfajor is a popular dessert in Latin America, especially in Argentina and Peru. It is often served at special occasions and celebrations.

w-mx-004.title: Arroz Poblano

instructions.1: Place the rice in a bowl with warm water and set aside for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, place the chopped onion, garlic clove, and 1/2 cup of cold water in a blender and process until you have a smooth mixture.
instructions.3: After 15 minutes, drain the water and rinse the rice with cold water until the water is clear. Make sure to drain well and shake off any excess water; it has to be as dry as possible.
instructions.4: Add vegetable oil to a saucepan or cazuela and place over medium-high heat. Heat the oil and add the rice. Fry the rice, stirring constantly until it becomes transparent, about 12 minutes. Use a spoon to drain any excess oil after this step.
instructions.5: Add the onion and garlic mixture to the rice and stir (be careful not to break the rice grains).
instructions.6: Add the hot water, parsley sprigs, and Serrano pepper (if using) and a few drops of lime juice.
instructions.7: When the water starts boiling, lower the heat to the lowest temperature, season with salt to taste, and cover the saucepan. Do not remove the lid.
instructions.8: After 20 minutes, the water should be absorbed almost completely. The rice should look cooked and soft. Remove from heat and let stand for about 10 minutes. Discard the parsley sprig and serve. The rice will continue to cook with its own heat.

w-mx-004.culturalNotes: Arroz Poblano is a traditional Mexican dish, known for its rich and subtle flavor.

w-mx-005.title: Mexican Barbacoa

instructions.1: In a large pot, place the onion, tomatillos, tomatoes, garlic, New Mexico chiles, and ancho chiles. Add 1 cup of water and bring the ingredients to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.2: Gently stir the ingredients and let them boil for 15 minutes until they become soft.
instructions.3: Add the lamb leg, agave nectar, and salt. Add 1/2 cup of water and let the lamb cook on low heat for 4 hours until it becomes tender and easy to shred.
instructions.4: In a small bowl, mix the Chile Colorado Sauce.
instructions.5: Warm the tortillas over medium heat until they become soft.
instructions.6: Serve the barbacoa with tortillas, sliced jicama, cubed avocados, Chile Colorado Sauce, chopped fresh cilantro, and lime wedges.

w-mx-005.culturalNotes: Barbacoa is a traditional Mexican dish typically made from lamb or beef and slow-cooked over low heat.

w-mx-006.title: Bolillo (Mexican Bread Rolls)

instructions.1: Prepare the yeast. In a cup or bowl, heat the water in the microwave or on the stove until it's warm (about 110-115°F). Add the yeast and sugar and mix. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let it stand for 5 minutes until it becomes foamy. If it doesn't become foamy, discard it and start again with a new packet of yeast.
instructions.2: Prepare the dough. In the bowl of a stand mixer (or a large bowl), whisk together the all-purpose flour and salt. Attach the dough hook to the mixer and add the oil and yeast mixture. Mix on medium-low speed for 6-8 minutes (or mix by hand) until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. If the dough is still fairly sticky, knead in 1 tablespoon of additional flour at a time until smooth and elastic. If it's too dry, add 1 tablespoon of additional water at a time.
instructions.3: Rise. Coat a large bowl with oil and transfer the dough to the bowl, shaping it into a ball. Cover it with a kitchen towel and let it rise until it has doubled in size, about 1-1.5 hours.
instructions.4: Shape and rise again. Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces and shape into 7-inch long ovals with a tapered end. Place 3 bolillos on each of the prepared baking sheets and lightly brush the tops with a little oil or spray with cooking spray to keep them moist. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise again for 45 minutes.
instructions.5: Preheat the oven. 15 minutes before they’re finished resting, fill a 9x13-inch baking dish with 10 cups of water and place it on the lowest rack in the oven to create a moist environment. Preheat the oven to 425°F.
instructions.6: Cut the bolillos. Make a ¼-inch deep cut lengthwise down the middle of each bolillo using a very sharp knife.
instructions.7: Bake. Spray the tops of the bolillos with a little water, then transfer them to the oven and bake for 30-35 minutes, until golden brown.
instructions.8: Let them cool for at least 10 minutes before serving.

w-mx-006.culturalNotes: Bolillo is a traditional Mexican bread used in many dishes such as tacos and sandwiches.

w-mx-007.title: Buñuelo

instructions.1: Make the Syrup: Dissolve the piloncillo and cinnamon stick in water until the sugar is melted. Let it cool.
instructions.2: Make the Topping: Mix sugar and ground cinnamon (if using).
instructions.3: Make the Dough: In a bowl, mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. Add water and melted oil, butter, or margarine and knead until the dough is smooth.
instructions.4: Shape the Dough: Roll out the dough and cut it into circles or small shapes.
instructions.5: Fry the Buñuelos: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the buñuelos until golden brown.
instructions.6: Serve: Drain the buñuelos on paper towels and serve hot with the syrup and topping.

w-mx-007.culturalNotes: Buñuelo is a traditional Mexican sweet, often served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-mx-008.title: Caldo de Queso

instructions.1: Add the Anaheim peppers to a baking sheet and place under the broiler for 10 minutes until the skin is blackened and blistered, flipping halfway through.
instructions.2: Remove the baking sheet from the broiler and cover it with aluminum foil or plastic wrap. Let it sit for 10 minutes. Uncover and remove as much of the skin from the peppers as possible.
instructions.3: Remove the stems and seeds, slice the peppers into strips, and set aside.
instructions.4: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Saute the onions and tomatoes for 5 minutes until the onions are translucent and the tomatoes start to soften.
instructions.5: Stir in the garlic and continue cooking for an additional minute, until fragrant.
instructions.6: Add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.7: Add the chicken broth, salt, and Mexican oregano. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook for 10 minutes, until the potatoes are fork tender.
instructions.8: Reduce the heat to low and add the whole milk, sliced Anaheim peppers, queso panela or queso fresco, and stir to combine. Cook uncovered for an additional 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
instructions.9: Serve immediately in bowls with corn tortillas, flour tortillas, bolillo bread, or your favorite salsa.

w-mx-008.culturalNotes: Caldo de Queso is a popular dish in Mexico, often served as a light meal or lunch.

w-mx-009.title: Caldo Tlalpeño

w-mx-009-i9.name: carrots
w-mx-009-i9.standardAmount: 2 carrots, peeled and sliced into half-moons

instructions.1: Add the chicken thighs, water, onion, garlic, salt, and bay leaves to a large pot or Dutch oven. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
instructions.2: Transfer the chicken to a bowl to cool, discard the bay leaves, and transfer the cooked onions and garlic into a blender. Strain and reserve the remaining broth in a large bowl.
instructions.3: In the blender with the cooked onions and garlic, add 1 cup of the reserved chicken broth, the tomatoes, salt, and chipotle pepper in adobo sauce. Blend until smooth.
instructions.4: Heat the olive oil in the same large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 more minutes until softened and translucent.
instructions.5: Pour in the blended tomato mixture and cook for an additional 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.6: While the tomato mixture cooks, shred the chicken thighs.
instructions.7: Add the shredded chicken, green beans, chickpeas, remaining chicken broth, epazote leaves, and cilantro sprigs to the pot. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Cook for 8 minutes until the green beans are tender. Taste and season with more salt if needed.
instructions.8: Serve immediately in bowls and garnish with a chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, crumbled queso fresco, sliced avocados, and chopped cilantro.

w-mx-009.culturalNotes: Caldo Tlalpeño is a traditional Mexican soup, often served in a traditional clay bowl.

w-mx-010.title: Capirotada (Mexican Bread Pudding)

w-mx-010-i6.name: shredded cheese (Longhorn Cheddar, Colby, or cheese of your choice)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
instructions.2: Cut the rolls into 1/2 inch slices and butter both sides, then place them on a baking sheet and bake for 3 minutes on each side until lightly toasted and dry. Remove and let cool.
instructions.3: Combine the water, piloncillo, cinnamon sticks, and cloves in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and let steep, covered, for 2 hours. Strain the liquid and discard the cinnamon sticks and cloves.
instructions.4: Spray an 8 x 10 1/2” baking dish with non-stick spray, then layer the ingredients in the following order: a third of the toasted bread, a third of the raisins, a third of the cheese, and 1 1/2 cups of the syrup. Wait 15 minutes, then layer another third of the bread, raisins, cheese, and syrup. Let it soak for another 15 minutes, and again top with the remaining bread, raisins, cheese, and syrup. Let it set for another 15 minutes before baking.
instructions.5: Cover the dish with aluminum foil that has been sprayed with non-stick spray and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake until the cheese is golden brown, about 10 to 15 minutes more. Serve warm.

w-mx-010.culturalNotes: Capirotada is a traditional Mexican dessert served during Lent. It is known for its sweet and savory flavor and its crunchy and moist texture.
